lyrics:
Damn. Be right back

Before you say anything — I tried the bottle
Winn-Dixie locked the door the second I walked out
There was a Coke in the console, maybe twelve ounces
I had a container. I had a plan. I had no doubt
I sat behind the wheel and told myself, "Hold on."
I've said that all my life. It's always worked for me
Turns out there's a statute of limitations—

TED

I'm explaining the physics
So I opened the door to improve the trajectory
Missed the bottle. Hit the seat. Minor collateral damage

NO

I said minor
Then the bottle hit the pavement and rolled under the car
At that point, Linda, the negotiation was over

WHAT

Nature made the ruling. I merely complied
And naturally, that's when a patrol car drove by

Now tell me who the victim was
The pavement didn't file a plea
They call it a victimless crime
but if there was a victim, it was me

Free to pee, free to pee
My own body turned on me
No one hurt, no property
So why ain't I free to pee
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee)
That's all I'm asking
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee)
A little understanding
Free to pee

Now take the dog next door. Explain him
He lifts one leg against my mailbox every day
Nobody cuffs him, nobody cites him
somebody scratches his head and calls him "good boy" anyway
A horse can let go right in the street
A pigeon drops evidence from thirty feet
But a man obeys the same command—

TED

I'm discussing equal treatment under the law
You can write an ordinance, laminate it, frame it —
nature never signed a thing
Nature never saw your zoning map
Nature never read the code
And when nature serves the summons
brother, somebody's gotta go

Free to pee, free to pee
Nature don't need a permit from me
Dog gets praise, I get a fee—
Tell me where's the equity
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee)
It's basic biology
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee)
Not public anarchy
I didn't choose the time
I didn't choose the place
I simply answered nature
and got paperwork in my face
FREE TO PEE

And who decides what's decent anyway
Some committee sitting downtown over coffee
Were any of them standing in that parking lot
Did anybody bother asking me

NO

Exactly
Nature gives me orders. That's bad enough
Now City Hall wants jurisdiction too
One says, "Go!"
The other says, "Don't!"
And somehow I'm the one who's supposed to know what to do
You regulate parking
You regulate signs
You regulate what day they pick up the trash
But when nature bangs the gavel, gentlemen
your little ordinance can kiss my—

TED

…constitutional ass

Before there was a courthouse
before there was a code
a man drank water
and sooner or later, he had to go
That's not rebellion
That's not depravity
That's water, patience, gravity —
the original authority
And don't you laugh, Linda
Fifty-eight has humbled better men than me

TED

I'm saying nature has seniority

I wasn't always a man who needed a plan

Ted

FREE TO PEE

(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee!)
FREE TO PEE
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee!)
No board, no badge, bureaucracy
gets seniority over biology
Call it indecent, charge your fee —
you cannot legislate necessity
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee!)
From every dog and every tree
(Free-ee-ee-ee to pee-ee-ee-ee!)
A basic human liberty
I tried the bottle
I tried the seat
I fought the law and the law fought me
So raise your voice for dignity —
FREE
TO
PEE

Ted

…I know

…
Damn. Be right back

impression.text: This highly energetic track bursts with a theatrical, comedic rock opera atmosphere, characterized by a bombastic arrangement of brass, electric guitars, and driving percussion. The production is exceptionally dense and polished, filling the stereo field with a lush hybrid of orchestral elements and modern rock instrumentation. Within this tightly packed mix, crisp and upfront lead vocals sit clearly above a heavily layered backing choir to ensure the humorous lyrics remain the focal point. Dramatic shifts between conversational narrative interjections and soaring, anthemic choral hooks define the quirky structure of the arrangement. A charismatic male vocal delivers the performance with immense theatricality, culminating in an abrupt spoken outro that perfectly captures the lively, stage-ready essence of the song.

review.review_text: Here is Rose the comic who has been hiding inside Rose the diarist all along, and "Free To Pee" is a full-blown one-act farce set to a brisk 3/4 that never once invites you to waltz. The whole thing hangs on the tension between Ted's escalating legal defense and Linda, whose entire vocabulary is a barked "TED!" landing on a sax-and-synth stab: the negotiation, the physics, the improved trajectory, all delivered with the wounded dignity of a man arguing before a court that does not exist. The doo-wop chorus turning martial by the second pass is the joke doing double duty, and the bridge is where it earns its keep, when the band drops to organ and bass and Ted goes philosopher: "That's water, patience, gravity, the original authority," then "Fifty-eight has humbled better men than me." There is real craft in how the outro cuts everything dead and loops back to that opening "Damn. Be right back," a punchline that reframes the whole five minutes as a bit Ted has clearly run before. It is broad, and a few of the stop-start verses run longer than the gag strictly needs, so this is one for the room rather than the headphones; but as a piece of theater it holds the floor and knows exactly what it is.
